TRANSITION PROVISIONS. The transition from the 4 use of motor vehicle registration plates on both the front and 5 rear of certain vehicles to the use of such plates on only 6 the rear of certain vehicles, as directed by this division of 7 this Act, shall be accomplished in stages. A person applying 8 for a new or replacement registration plate on or after the 9 effective date of this division of this Act shall receive only 10 one registration plate. Otherwise, the transition shall not 11 be accomplished until a new series of registration plates is 12 issued to replace a current series. A person who was issued 13 a pair of registration plates, including special registration 14 plates, may attach only one plate in accordance with this 15 division of this Act on and after the effective date of this 16 division of this Act. A person who is required to transfer a 17 registration plate, or to return a registration plate to the 18 department of transportation or to a county treasurer, shall 19 transfer or return both plates, as applicable, if the person 20 was issued a pair of plates. Section 321.438, subsection 2, Code 2026, is 26 amended to read as follows: 27 2. a. A person shall not operate on the highway a motor 28 vehicle equipped with a front windshield, a side window to the 29 immediate right or left of the driver, or a sidewing forward 30 of and to the left or right of the driver which is excessively 31 dark or reflective so that it is difficult for a person outside 32 the motor vehicle to see into the motor vehicle through the 33 windshield, window, or sidewing that meets a minimum standard 34 of transparency of less than fifty percent light transmittance . 35 -7- LSB 5770YC (3) 91 th/ns 7/ 9 H.F. _____ a. The department shall adopt rules establishing a minimum 1 measurable standard of transparency which shall apply to 2 violations of this subsection . 3 b. This subsection does not apply to a person who operates 4 a motor vehicle owned or leased by a federal, state, or local 5 law enforcement agency if the operation is part of the person’s 6 official duties. 7 EXPLANATION 8 The inclusion of this explanation does not constitute agreement with 9 the explanation’s substance by the members of the general assembly. 10 ISSUANCE AND DISPLAY OF ONE REGISTRATION PLATE. Under 11 current law, two registration plates are issued for a motor 12 vehicle other than an autocycle, motorcycle, motorized bicycle, 13 or truck tractor, and are required to be attached to the 14 front and rear of the vehicle. This bill provides that only 15 one registration plate must be issued for a motor vehicle. 16 The registration plate must be attached to the rear of the 17 motor vehicle, except that the registration plate for a truck 18 tractor must be attached to the front of the truck tractor, in 19 accordance with current law. 20 The bill also makes corresponding changes, directs the 21 Code editor to make necessary changes, and provides for the 22 transition from the use of two registration plates to the 23 use of one registration plate. A person who was issued two 24 registration plates is authorized to attach only one plate, in 25 accordance with the bill, on and after the effective date of 26 the bill, and must transfer or return both plates if a transfer 27 or return is required. 28 WINDOW TINT. Under current law, a person is prohibited from 29 operating a motor vehicle equipped with a front windshield, a 30 side window to the immediate right or left of the driver, or 31 a sidewing forward of and to the left or right of the driver 32 (window) which is excessively dark or reflective so that it is 33 difficult for a person outside the motor vehicle to see into 34 the motor vehicle through the window. Under rules adopted 35 -8- LSB 5770YC (3) 91 th/ns 8/ 9 H.F. _____ by the department of transportation (DOT) (761 IAC 450.5), 1 “excessively dark or reflective” means the window does not 2 meet a minimum standard of transparency of 70 percent light 3 transmittance. However, the requirement does not apply to 4 a person who operates a motor vehicle owned or leased by 5 a federal, state, or local law enforcement agency if the 6 operation is part of the person’s official duties. 7 The bill strikes the authority of the DOT to adopt rules 8 establishing a minimum measurable standard of transparency 9 and instead prohibits a person from operating on the highway 10 a motor vehicle equipped with a window that meets a minimum 11 standard of transparency of less than 50 percent light 12 transmittance. 13 A violation of Code section 321.438 is punishable by a 14 scheduled fine of $70. 15 -9- LSB 5770YC (3) 91 th/ns 9/ 9
